claims.text: The local release and selected snapshot preserve the ANA Get in a Jet! Double Chance Campaign source slice as November 1, 1998 through January 31, 1999, while also preserving a Bulbapedia rendered-table wording caveat that says November 1-31, 1998.

The selected snapshot identifies the distribution context as All Nippon Airways / All Nippon Airlines Get in a Jet! Double Chance Campaign and source-pins Flying Pikachu and Dragonite to that campaign.

The local release models two currently source-pinned card identities in this child slice: Flying Pikachu row 051 and Dragonite row 052. It does not model redemption forms, flight/customer records, official copy counts, or a complete ANA promo census.

The local rows credit both Flying Pikachu and Dragonite to Toshinao Aoki as source-provider metadata; the selected snapshot directly surfaces a Toshinao Aoki label for Dragonite. Treat the artist claim as catalog texture, not physical-card authentication.

This source group matters because airline travel becomes part of Pokemon's collectible assembly: Flying Pikachu makes the flight motif literal, while Dragonite gives the campaign an older, gentle carrier energy.

Agents must preserve ANA/Get in a Jet route, row 051/052 identities, date-wording caveat, Aoki source-provider credit, and distinguish this slice from CoroCoro Flying Pikachu, Game Boy/Fossil/Rocket/VS Dragonite rows, ANA postcard or airline merch objects, and later travel Pikachu memories.

narrative.human_title: ANA Get in a Jet! — Pokemon as airline memory
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those promo slices where the object smells like the outside world. Pokemon was not only in binders and magazines; it was in airlines, travel campaigns, and the fantasy of being carried somewhere. Flying Pikachu is the obvious icon, but Dragonite is the soul of the route: friendly, heavy, airborne, and exactly the kind of creature you would trust with a journey.
